source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: Structures for adjectival predication without buol ‘be’ (present tense)
notes: The DP subject ehigi ‘you (pl.)’ is predicated inside AP of a bare adjective. It then moves to Spec,IP where I acquires a [2pl] feature which is later spelled out as –ŋyt. The adjective does not raise to I (on Infl and movement see section 4.2.1.6). To derive the right word order, two XP-frontings take place: first the AP to Spec,FP (suggestive of Focus Phrase), then the subject to Spec,TopP (mnemonic of Topic Phrase).
